newsitem.title: INDIA: India's Congress party elects Kesri to succeed Rao.
newsitem.headline: India's Congress party elects Kesri to succeed Rao.

text.p: India's Congress party on Monday elected veteran leader Sitaram Kesri as its provisional president to take the place of former Prime Minister P.V. Narasimha Rao, the United News of India (UNI) said.

The news agency quoted party sources as saying Kesri was elected by the party's elite Congress Working Committee (CWC) to be interim president after the departure of Rao, who resigned on Saturday after a court summons in a criminal conspiracy case.

A senior party leader confirmed to Reuters towards the close of the CWC meeting that Kesri would be a stopgap president pending the election of a new chief by the All India Congress Committee, the powerful plenary of the party, which is expected to meet sometime next month.

Rao resigned after a Delhi judge asked him to testify in the "cheating" case which involves a business magnate who alleges he paid $100,000 to a Rao acquaintance in 1983 in a failed attempt to win a government contract.
Kesri, party treasurer since 1979, is widely seen as a man acceptable to warring factions of the fractious party, which has ruled India for all but four years since independence from Britain in 1947.

The party has been plagued this year by a series of corruption scandals involving its senior leaders, and turned in its worst electoral performance when it was defeated in the general elections held in April and May this year.
